findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

Approved with warnings. The fix is small and narrowly scoped. `requireIdentical` now does a stable sort of the union of keys in three tiers: non-`.project/` `file:`/`mode:` keys first, then `.project/` `file:`/`mode:` keys, then everything else (aggregate, dependency and tool keys). Every key is still compared, so no stale or refusal decision is weakened; only which changed input gets named first is different. `key.slice(5)` is correct because both `file:` and `mode:` are five characters long. `toSorted` is stable, so the original order is kept within each tier. This fixes the root cause in the investigation note. Editing a required assertion source changes the reader identity, which turns off audit projection. That makes both audit-ticket digests differ even though their bytes did not change, and the old order named `.project/` first. Now the only changed raw product key, `file:packages/cli/tests/integration/planning-scope-review.test.ts`, is named first. The existing Cucumber assertion matches that exact path, so it can tell the fix from the old behaviour, as the retained RED shows. The cucumber config only selects the feature file and imports the step definitions. It changes no repository-wide tags. I found nothing that causes a concrete release failure. The remaining concerns are about proof I can't see, not about defects.

The packet has no GREEN run. The trusted RED (review b7a05540) shows the source-edit currency row failing on the wrong path, but there is no rerun proving it now passes. There is also no rerun proving the other three currency rows and the full feature still pass after the reorder. Before any GREEN credit is claimed, retain the GREEN execution of features/observe-bounded-delivery-proof.feature:99 and its sibling rows.

`audit-readers.json` pins `source_sha256` to a digest of every tracked non-`.project/`, non-plugin file, so editing `index.ts` forces this value to change. I can't check the new value from this packet. If it is wrong, `permitsAuditProjection` silently returns false. The Work Log and audit-summary currency rows would then report stale instead of current, and the cause would be hard to find. Because the pin depends on all source bytes, every future source edit needs it regenerated. A dedicated check that recomputes and compares the value would turn a confusing currency failure into a named one.

The accepted-scope currency row expects 'Changed accepted scope' plus 'review an updated shipped contract'. Under the new order, a committed scope edit to a T3E4NS ticket gets priority 1, and `requireIdentical` would report 'Changed input file:.project/...; observe the new committed candidate'. So that row can only pass if `validateCandidateContract` (contract.ts, not supplied) refuses earlier inside `currentInputs`, with the scope-specific message. This change doesn't affect that path, but it isn't shown here, and this row needs its own GREEN evidence.

When several inputs change at once, the error still names only the first one. The new order picks a raw product file over derived ticket projections or tool/dependency identities, which fits the R4 recovery action. A raw edit to a `.project/` file that is not an audit ticket is now reported after any `packages/` change. That is acceptable, because both lead to the same 'observe the new committed candidate' action.
